Parse JSON text with Glaze

Source: R/json.R
fromJSON.Rd

JSON objects become named lists, arrays become lists or, when simplified, atomic vectors, matrices and data frames. JSON null becomes NULL, or NA inside a simplified vector, matrix or data frame.

Usage

fromJSON(
  txt,
  simplifyVector = TRUE,
  simplifyDataFrame = simplifyVector,
  simplifyMatrix = simplifyVector
)

Arguments

txt

A length-one JSON string. If it names an existing file, that file is read with jsonlite::read_json().

simplifyVector

Simplify arrays of scalar values to atomic vectors.

simplifyDataFrame

Simplify arrays of records to data frames. Has no effect unless simplifyVector is also TRUE.

simplifyMatrix

Simplify regular arrays of arrays to matrices and higher-dimensional arrays. Has no effect unless simplifyVector is also TRUE.

Value

An R object: a named list for a JSON object; a list, atomic vector, matrix, array or data frame for a JSON array; a length-one vector for a JSON scalar; and NULL for JSON null.

Simplification

With simplifyVector = TRUE, an array whose elements are all strings, all booleans or all numbers (apart from null) becomes a character, logical, integer or double vector. Numbers are integers when every one of them is a whole number that fits R's integer type, and doubles otherwise. Arrays that mix these types, contain objects, or contain only null stay lists.

With simplifyMatrix = TRUE, arrays of equally long arrays of scalars of one type become a matrix, with one row per inner array. Deeper regular nestings become arrays of three or more dimensions. This reverses what jsonlite::toJSON() writes for a matrix or an array.

With simplifyDataFrame = TRUE, an array of objects becomes a data frame when every field holds scalars of one type. Fields missing from a record are NA. Arrays of objects with nested or mixed-type fields stay lists of records.

See also

jsonlite::toJSON() for the reverse conversion, jsonlite::read_json() to parse a file.

Examples

fromJSON('{"id": 1, "tags": ["a", "b"], "ok": true}')
#> $id
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $tags
#> [1] "a" "b"
#> 
#> $ok
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
fromJSON('[1, 2.5, null]')
#> [1] 1.0 2.5  NA
fromJSON('[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]')
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    1    2    3
#> [2,]    4    5    6
fromJSON('[{"id": 1, "name": "A"}, {"id": 2, "name": "B"}]')
#>   id name
#> 1  1    A
#> 2  2    B
fromJSON('[{"id": 1}, {"id": 2}]', simplifyDataFrame = FALSE)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$id
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$id
#> [1] 2
#> 
#>
